pages.text: "Slowpoke! Sonu's a slowpoke!" Mina stamped in the yard. Low river water exposed a long flight of steps. Round-bellied little Sonu waddled far behind.
"Let's race around the yard!" Mina wanted to run with Sonu. Sonu shook their head and sat beside the tub. "That's because you're a slowpoke!" Mina shouted again.
Sonu stood before the goat, stamped, and called, "Slowpoke! Slowpoke!" Mina's words came exactly from Sonu's mouth. The goat stopped chewing and looked up.
"Stop!" Mina said. "Stop! Slowpoke!" Sonu copied. The race had not even started. Mina stood alone in the big yard.
Pouring water into the tub, Mom called Mina. "Sonu learns your words. What would you like to teach?" Mina gently touched their mouth.
Mina crouched before Sonu. "I'm sorry about earlier. You're a strong one!" Sonu's eyes widened. "Strong one?"
Sonu went around the yard calling, "Strong one! Sonu's a strong one!" Again, Mina's words came from Sonu. Mina smiled. "Kind Words Teach Kind Words!"
Mom asked, "Shall you run together this time?" Mina stood beside Sonu. "Slow is fine. Let's go together!"
They went once around the yard. Waiting, Mina waved. "You made it here!" Sonu smiled.
Mom hugged them at her sides. "Run with me tomorrow, too," Mina said. Sonu smiled and copied, "Run with me!"
